Maria (infra): heads-up — we’re seeing a persistent skew in traffic across endpoints for model-serving in us-west-2. 30-40% of requests are getting routed to the same subset of pods and causing retries 
Kevin (sre): interesting, metrics show retry rate up and per-node tcp retransmits too. Any recent kernel/network changes on that cluster? :thinking_face: 
Raj (eng-runtime): not from our side. We rolled a config tweak to kube-proxy last week (ipvs sync-period) but that was minor. timeline matches? 
Maria (infra): sync-period change was 2d ago, spikes started ~4h ago. also saw a lot of ICMP fragmentation logs from the RDMA nodes earlier. 
Josh (network): can you paste ipvs state and endpoint weights? run: `sudo ipvsadm -Ln --stats` and `kubectl get endpoints -o wide svc/model-infer` 
Maria (infra): pasted output below 
```
IPVS connections:
TCP  10.10.32.1:8080 rr
  -> 10.244.0.12:8080            Masq    1      0          0
  -> 10.244.1.23:8080            Masq    7      0          0
  -> 10.244.2.45:8080            Masq    2      0          0
```
Endpoints show two nodes with weight 7 and 1 etc. 
Kevin (sre): that weight distribution is weird. ipvs should be using equal weights unless kube-proxy/node annotation changed. Check `/var/lib/kube-proxy/config.conf` on nodes and ipvs scheduler. 
Raj (eng-runtime): also worth checking MTU on the RDMA interface — fragmentation can change hash inputs and skew flows. `ip link show` on the app NICs? 
Maria (infra): `ip link` shows eth0 mtu 1500 on app nodes but mlx5 RDMA nodes are 9000. There’s an MTU mismatch across nodes serving the same service. 
Josh (network): there you go — path MTU differences can cause IPVS hashing to prefer certain endpoints (packets getting fragmented/reshaped). combined with conn reuse it can steer new connections. 
Kevin (sre): quick mitigation: set ipvs scheduler to rr? or adjust weights to equalize until we fix MTU. `ipvsadm -e --scheduler rr` — but that’s disruptive. 
Raj (eng-runtime): we can patch kube-proxy to set equal weights via endpointslice controller, non-disruptive. I'll push a 1-line change to adjust `targetWeight` normalization. 
Maria (infra): rolling a config to force equal weights now on a canary node. 
infra-bot: deploy/cfg-update model-infer-weight-normalize to eng-infra-canary started by Raj (eng-runtime) — started at 1876543400 
Kevin (sre): monitoring — looking at node-level tx/rx errors, conntrack entries, and ipvs counters. if retries drop after canary we'll roll global. 
Maria (infra): canary looks promising, retries down from 38% -> 6% on that az after weight-normalize and a quick mtu fix on one misconfigured node. 
Josh (network): next step: audit IaC for MTU and RDMA NIC settings, ensure all nodes in the same LB pool have consistent MTU and offload settings. I'll open a runbook. :clipboard: 
Raj (eng-runtime): also adding a post-deploy check in our rollout that validates ipvs weights and `ip link` MTU across endpoints for the service. 
Maria (infra): thanks team. followup actions: 1) schedule MTU reconciliation across RDMA/app nodes, 2) rollout weight-normalize for all clusters, 3) add automated check to rollout pipeline, 4) postmortem if we see regression. 
Kevin (sre): +1. tagging #oncall to watch for any residual flapping. :eyes:
Maria (infra): closing thread for now, will reopen if anything else pops up.
